answer: A key earns only what a stranger pays for. Anyone outside the membership may buy a piece of work (a sonnet, a fable, a study in umber), and the ledger mints a subsidy worth 0.6 of the buyer's signed receipt, in real currency, tied to one buyer and one work digest. Receipts redeem once; refunds reverse the mint; a duplicate sale is provable theft and voids the balance. So a thousand clones earn nothing until a thousand strangers pay, and each sale returns less than it cost, losing forty cents a cycle. Growth is capped by customers, not by keys.
